question: Which of the following is an example of direct tax?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Income Tax.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A direct tax is a tax whose burden cannot be shifted to another person; it is paid directly by the individual or entity on whom it is levied, based on income or wealth. Income Tax is the most common example of a direct tax in India. (आयकर — प्रत्यक्ष कर)

 

• Direct taxes in India are governed mainly by the Income Tax Act, 1961, and are administered by the Central Board of Direct Taxes (CBDT).

 

• Other examples of direct taxes include Corporate Tax, Wealth Tax (abolished 2015), and Capital Gains Tax.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Indirect taxes (like GST, Customs Duty) are levied on goods and services, and their burden can be shifted from the person paying to the final consumer.

 

• India's major indirect tax reform, the Goods and Services Tax (GST), was implemented on 1 July 2017, subsuming most central and state indirect taxes.

 

NOTE

 

• Escheat (Option 1): This is not a tax; it is the legal principle by which the state acquires ownership of property that has no living heirs or claimants.

 

• Custom Duty (Option 3): This is an indirect tax levied on goods imported into or exported out of the country.

 

• Goods and Services Tax (Option 4): This is an indirect tax levied on the supply of goods and services, ultimately borne by the end consumer.

question:
In India which of the following statements regarding Fundamental Duty is NOT correct?

1. Total number of Fundamental Duties are 11

2. Article 51-A is related to Fundamental Duties

3. Inserted by 43rd Constitutional Amendment

4. Incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution
option_1: Total number of Fundamental Duties are 11
option_2: Article 51-A is related to Fundamental Duties
option_4: Incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution
solution_text:
The correct answer is Inserted by 43rd Constitutional Amendment.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Fundamental Duties were added to the Indian Constitution by the 42nd Constitutional Amendment Act, 1976, on the recommendation of the Swaran Singh Committee — not by the 43rd Amendment. (मूल कर्तव्य — 42वां संविधान संशोधन)

 

• They are listed under Article 51-A, contained in the newly inserted Part IV-A of the Constitution.

 

• Originally there were 10 Fundamental Duties; the 86th Constitutional Amendment Act, 2002 added an 11th Fundamental Duty (a parent/guardian's duty to provide opportunities for education to their child/ward between ages 6-14), bringing the total to 11.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Fundamental Duties are inspired by the Constitution of the erstwhile USSR (Russia).

 

• Unlike Fundamental Rights, Fundamental Duties are not justiciable, i.e., they cannot be directly enforced by courts.

 

NOTE

 

• Total number of Fundamental Duties are 11 (Option 1): This statement is correct — after the 86th Amendment (2002) added one more duty, the total became 11.

 

• Article 51-A is related to Fundamental Duties (Option 2): This statement is correct — Article 51-A enumerates all the Fundamental Duties.

 

• Incorporated in Part IV-A of the Constitution (Option 4): This statement is correct — Fundamental Duties are contained in Part IV-A, added by the 42nd Amendment.

question: Which of these conditions enhance the potential of MFIs to attract more resources and expand services to their clients?
option_3: Ability to disintegrate from communities they operate in
option_4: Ability to lend large amounts of loans
solution_text:
The correct answer is Financially viable and self-sustaining MFIs.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Micro-Finance Institutions (MFIs) are organisations that provide small-scale financial services — credit, savings, insurance — to low-income individuals or groups who lack access to conventional banking. (सूक्ष्म वित्त संस्थान — वित्तीय रूप से टिकाऊ)

 

• When MFIs are financially viable and self-sustaining, they can operate profitably without relying on continuous subsidies or donor support, which builds credibility and helps them attract more commercial funding and resources from banks, investors, and capital markets.

 

• Financial sustainability also enables MFIs to scale up operations and expand the range and reach of services to a larger client base.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• MFIs in India are regulated by the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) as Non-Banking Financial Company-Micro Finance Institutions (NBFC-MFIs).

 

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, pioneered by NABARD, is one of the largest microfinance models in the world.

 

NOTE

 

• Access to foreign aid (Option 2): Excessive dependence on foreign aid can make an MFI less self-reliant and does not by itself build sustainable resource-attracting capacity.

 

• Ability to disintegrate from communities they operate in (Option 3): MFIs need strong ties with the communities they serve to build trust; disintegrating from communities would weaken, not enhance, their potential.

 

• Ability to lend large amounts of loans (Option 4): Microfinance is characterised by small-ticket loans; lending large amounts is not a defining feature that enhances an MFI's resource-attracting potential.

question: How many countries are part of SAARC?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 8.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The South Asian Association for Regional Cooperation (SAARC) has 8 member countries: India, Pakistan, Bangladesh, Nepal, Bhutan, Sri Lanka, Maldives, and Afghanistan. (सार्क — 8 सदस्य देश)

 

• SAARC was established on 8 December 1985 in Dhaka, Bangladesh.

 

• Its Secretariat is located in Kathmandu, Nepal, and became operational in 1987.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Afghanistan joined SAARC in 2007 as its eighth member, at the 14th SAARC Summit.

 

• SAARC also has 9 observer states, including China, the USA, and the European Union.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 2, 3 and 4 (2, 5 and 7) are incorrect as none of them matches SAARC's actual membership count of 8.

question: Chaitrual and Phulaich are the festival of which of the following states?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Himachal Pradesh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Chaitrual and Phulaich (the flower festival) are traditional festivals celebrated in the tribal Kinnaur region of Himachal Pradesh. (फुलैच — हिमाचल प्रदेश का पुष्प उत्सव)

 

• Phulaich is celebrated to pay tribute to departed ancestors, with people decorating their homes and offering flowers gathered from high mountain slopes.

 

• Chaitrual marks the local New Year/onset of spring in the tribal belt of Himachal Pradesh and is celebrated with traditional rituals and community gatherings.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other notable festivals of Himachal Pradesh include Kullu Dussehra, Losar (Tibetan New Year, celebrated in Lahaul-Spiti and Kinnaur), and the Minjar Fair of Chamba.

 

NOTE

 

• Gujarat (Option 2): Known for festivals like Navratri, Rann Utsav, and Uttarayan (Kite Festival).

 

• Uttarakhand (Option 3): Known for festivals like Kumbh Mela (Haridwar), Nanda Devi Raj Jat, and Harela.

 

• Haryana (Option 4): Known for festivals like Gugga Naumi and Baisakhi.

question: Which of the following erstwhile Princely states was primarily associated with Kathak?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Avadh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kathak, one of the eight classical dance forms of India, flourished under the patronage of the Nawabs of Avadh (Oudh), centred at Lucknow, giving rise to the famous Lucknow Gharana of Kathak. (कथक नृत्य — अवध/लखनऊ घराना)

 

• The word 'Kathak' is derived from 'Katha', meaning story, and 'Kathakars' were traditionally storytellers who narrated tales through dance, music and expressions.

 

• Under Nawab Wajid Ali Shah of Avadh, a great patron of arts, Kathak was refined into a highly sophisticated court art form, with emphasis on intricate footwork (tatkar), spins (chakkars), and expressive gestures (abhinaya).

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The other major Kathak Gharana is the Jaipur Gharana, which developed under the patronage of the Rajasthani royal court and emphasises vigorous footwork and pure dance (nritta).

 

• The Benaras Gharana of Kathak is a smaller, distinct tradition centred on Varanasi.

 

NOTE

 

• Tripura (Option 1): Known for folk dances such as Hojagiri, not Kathak.

 

• Baroda (Option 3): The Gaekwad rulers of Baroda were notable patrons of Hindustani classical music, not primarily Kathak.

 

• Vijaynagar (Option 4): The Vijayanagara Empire is associated with the development of Carnatic music and temple dance traditions in South India, not Kathak.

question:
Identify the INCORRECT statement/s concerning SHGs.

i. They include voluntary groups of up to 20 socially and economically homogenous people.

ii. There is no need to follow the well-defined rules and bye-laws for SHGs.

iii. In April 1996, RBI declared SHG-BLP as a priority sector lending activity.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Only ii.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Self-Help Group (SHG) is a voluntary group of about 10 to 20 socially and economically homogenous people who come together to address common issues through mutual savings and credit. (स्वयं सहायता समूह — 10 से 20 सदस्य)

 

• Statement i is correct: SHGs are indeed voluntary groups of up to 20 socially and economically homogenous members, as per NABARD's SHG guidelines.

 

• Statement ii is incorrect: A well-functioning SHG is in fact expected to follow well-defined rules and bye-laws, hold regular meetings, and maintain proper books of accounts — this is one of the recognised characteristics of a good, sustainable SHG, contrary to what the statement claims.

 

• Statement iii is correct: In April 1996, the RBI advised banks to consider lending to SHGs (SHG-Bank Linkage Programme, or SHG-BLP) as part of their mainstream credit/priority sector lending operations, mainstreaming the pilot programme NABARD had launched in 1992.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The SHG-Bank Linkage Programme (SBLP) was piloted by NABARD in 1992 and is one of the largest microfinance outreach programmes in the world.

 

• SHGs typically maintain small common funds through voluntary thrift/savings by members, which are then used to make small interest-bearing loans within the group.

 

NOTE

 

• ii and iii (Option 1): Incorrect because statement iii is factually correct, not incorrect.

 

• Only i (Option 2): Incorrect because statement i is factually correct, not incorrect.

 

• Only iii (Option 3): Incorrect because statement iii is factually correct, while statement ii is the one that is actually incorrect.

question: Use of more labour and capital inputs on the given land under cultivation is referred to as __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is intensive cultivation.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Intensive cultivation refers to a farming method in which more labour and capital are applied to a given (fixed) piece of land in order to increase output per unit area. (गहन कृषि — अधिक श्रम व पूंजी का उपयोग)

 

• It typically involves the use of high-yielding variety (HYV) seeds, fertilisers, irrigation, machinery, and more labour input to maximise productivity from limited land.

 

• Intensive cultivation is common in regions with high population density and limited availability of agricultural land, such as much of India's Gangetic plains.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• Extensive cultivation, in contrast, involves farming a larger area of land with relatively lower input of labour and capital per unit area, relying on the sheer size of land to increase total output.

 

• The Green Revolution in India (from the mid-1960s) is a major example of intensive cultivation practices being adopted at scale.

 

NOTE

 

• Extensive cultivation (Option 1): This involves cultivating a larger area with comparatively less labour/capital per unit of land — the opposite of the concept described.

 

• Hybrid cultivation (Option 3): Not a standard classification of cultivation intensity; it generally refers to the use of hybrid seed varieties.

 

• Capitalist cultivation (Option 4): Not a recognised economic classification of land-use intensity; this is a distractor option.

question: When was Kapil Dev awarded with Padma Shri Award?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 1982.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Kapil Dev, the legendary Indian cricketer and captain of India's 1983 Cricket World Cup-winning team, was awarded the Padma Shri, India's fourth-highest civilian award, in 1982. (कपिल देव — पद्म श्री 1982)

 

• He later went on to receive the Padma Bhushan (India's third-highest civilian award) in 1991.

 

• Kapil Dev was also honoured with the Wisden Cricketer of the Year award and was named "Indian Cricketer of the Century" by Wisden in 2002.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Kapil Dev famously led India to its first Cricket World Cup title in 1983, defeating the West Indies in the final at Lord's.

 

• He also holds the world record for being the first bowler to take 400+ Test wickets while also scoring 5000+ Test runs, an all-rounder milestone.

 

NOTE

 

• Options 1, 2 and 4 (1981, 1980 and 1983) are incorrect as they do not correspond to the actual year (1982) in which Kapil Dev received the Padma Shri.

question: What is the most generally used indicator of overall economic performance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Per capita Gross National Product.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Per capita Gross National Product (GNP) — the total value of goods and services produced by a country's residents (within and outside the country) divided by its population — is traditionally the most widely used single indicator of a country's overall economic performance. (प्रति व्यक्ति सकल राष्ट्रीय उत्पाद — आर्थिक प्रदर्शन का सूचक)

 

• It is used extensively by international bodies like the World Bank to classify countries into income groups (low-income, middle-income, high-income economies).

 

• Being an easily quantifiable, single monetary figure, GNP per capita allows straightforward cross-country and cross-time comparisons of economic output and income levels.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Human Development Index (HDI), published by the UNDP, is a broader, composite measure covering life expectancy, education, and per capita income — used to assess overall well-being/development rather than just economic performance.

 

• The Physical Quality of Life Index (PQLI), developed by Morris David Morris, combines literacy rate, infant mortality, and life expectancy to measure quality of life, excluding income altogether.

 

NOTE

 

• Human Development Index (Option 2): A composite social development index, not a pure economic-performance indicator.

 

• Physical Quality of Life Index (Option 3): Measures quality of life based on health and literacy, not economic output.

 

• Standard of living (Option 4): A broad, qualitative concept without a single standardised metric, unlike GNP per capita.

question: The analysis of the interrelationship between the economy and the environment in the economic environmental accounting system was put forward by __________.
solution_text:
The correct answer is United Nations Statistical Office.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The System of Environmental-Economic Accounting (SEEA), which analyses the interrelationship between the economy and the environment, was developed and put forward by the United Nations Statistical Office (now the UN Statistics Division). (पर्यावरण-आर्थिक लेखा प्रणाली — संयुक्त राष्ट्र सांख्यिकी कार्यालय)

 

• SEEA is designed as a satellite system to the System of National Accounts (SNA), integrating environmental data (natural resources, pollution, ecosystem services) with economic data.

 

• The SEEA Central Framework was adopted as the first international statistical standard for environmental-economic accounting by the UN Statistical Commission in 2012.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• India has been progressively adopting environmental accounting frameworks; the Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI) has been working on natural capital accounting in line with SEEA.

 

• The SEEA Ecosystem Accounting framework was adopted by the UN in 2021 as a further extension covering ecosystem extent, condition, and services.

 

NOTE

 

• Central Statistical Office (Option 1): India's national statistical body responsible for national income accounting, not the originator of the SEEA framework.

 

• National Environmental Engineering Institute (NEERI) (Option 2): An Indian research institute focused on environmental engineering, unrelated to devising environmental accounting systems.

 

• Directorate of Economics and Statistics (Option 3): A state/central-level statistical body in India, not the body that put forward the SEEA framework.

question: Who among the following was the disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Swami Vivekananda.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Swami Vivekananda (born Narendranath Datta) was the foremost disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa, and went on to found the Ramakrishna Mission in 1897 in his guru's honour. (स्वामी विवेकानंद — रामकृष्ण परमहंस के शिष्य)

 

• He famously represented Hinduism at the World's Parliament of Religions in Chicago in 1893, beginning his speech with "Sisters and Brothers of America."

 

• Vivekananda propagated the philosophy of Practical Vedanta, emphasising selfless service (seva) and spiritual strength; his birthday, 12 January, is observed as National Youth Day in India.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Ramakrishna Mission, headquartered at Belur Math near Kolkata, engages in humanitarian, educational, and spiritual work worldwide.

 

• Ramakrishna Paramahansa himself was a priest at the Dakshineswar Kali Temple near Kolkata and preached the harmony of all religions.

 

NOTE

 

• Swami Dayanand (Option 1): Founder of the Arya Samaj (1875); not a disciple of Ramakrishna Paramahansa.

 

• Swami Sahajnanada (Option 2): Founder of the Swaminarayan sect; unconnected to Ramakrishna Paramahansa.

 

• Swami Shraddhanand (Option 4): A prominent Arya Samaj reformer and freedom fighter, associated with Dayanand Saraswati's tradition, not Ramakrishna's.

question: Which National Waterway runs from Haldia to Prayagraj?
solution_text:
The correct answer is National Waterway 1.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• National Waterway 1 (NW-1) runs along the Ganga-Bhagirathi-Hooghly river system, covering a stretch of 1,620 km from Haldia (West Bengal) to Prayagraj (Uttar Pradesh). (राष्ट्रीय जलमार्ग 1 — हल्दिया से प्रयागराज)

 

• It is the longest National Waterway in India and is being developed under the Jal Marg Vikas Project (JMVP) with assistance from the World Bank.

 

• NW-1 connects major cities like Haldia, Kolkata, Bhagalpur, Patna, Varanasi, and Prayagraj, facilitating cargo movement and passenger transport.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAI), headquartered in Noida, is responsible for the development and regulation of National Waterways.

 

• Under the National Waterways Act, 2016, 111 waterways were declared as National Waterways in India.

 

NOTE

 

• National Waterway 2 (Option 1): Runs along the river Brahmaputra, from Sadiya to Dhubri in Assam.

 

• National Waterway 3 (Option 3): Runs along the West Coast Canal in Kerala (Kollam-Kottapuram), along with Champakara and Udyogmandal canals.

 

• National Waterway 4 (Option 4): Runs along the rivers Godavari and Krishna, along with certain canals, in Andhra Pradesh and Telangana.

question: Which of the following components is NOT related to the New India Literacy Programme?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Business and Enhancing skill Development.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The New India Literacy Programme (NILP), also known as ULLAS – Nav Bharat Saaksharta Karyakram, is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme (2022-2027) of the Ministry of Education, aimed at achieving universal foundational literacy and numeracy among non-literates aged 15 and above. (नव भारत साक्षरता कार्यक्रम — पांच घटक)

 

• It has five defined components: (i) Foundational Literacy and Numeracy, (ii) Critical Life Skills, (iii) Vocational Skills Development, (iv) Basic Education, and (v) Continuing Education.

 

• "Business and Enhancing Skill Development" is not one of NILP's officially defined components — the actual skill-related component is termed "Vocational Skills Development", making this option the odd one out.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• NILP targets covering 5 crore non-literates and is implemented mainly through volunteerism, using a mobile app and online teaching-learning materials (DIKSHA portal).

 

• Under this scheme, online self-assessment is conducted for learners twice a year through a common test conducted by NCERT/PSSCIVE, and a national assessment is also held.

 

NOTE

 

• Foundational Literacy and Numeracy (Option 2): This is one of the five genuine components of NILP, focused on basic reading, writing and numeracy skills.

 

• Critical Life Skills (Option 3): This is one of the five genuine components, covering skills like digital literacy, financial literacy, legal literacy, health awareness and civic literacy.

 

• Basic Education (Option 4): This is one of the five genuine components, providing equivalency to formal education levels (Class 3, 5, 8, etc.) for adult learners.

question: Which of the following rivers originates near Sihawa in Raipur district of Chhattisgarh, flows through Odisha, and eventually empties into the Bay of Bengal?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mahanadi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Mahanadi River originates near Sihawa in the Dhamtari/Raipur region of Chhattisgarh, flows through Chhattisgarh and Odisha, and empties into the Bay of Bengal. (महानदी — सिहावा, छत्तीसगढ़ से उद्गम)

 

• It has a total length of about 858 km and is one of the major peninsular rivers of India, known for periodic devastating floods, earning it the nickname "Sorrow of Odisha".

 

• The Hirakud Dam, one of the longest dams in the world, is built across the Mahanadi River near Sambalpur, Odisha.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Major tributaries of the Mahanadi include the Seonath, Hasdeo, Mand, Ib, and Tel rivers.

 

• The Mahanadi basin covers parts of Chhattisgarh, Odisha, Jharkhand, Madhya Pradesh, and Maharashtra.

 

NOTE

 

• Krishna (Option 2): Originates near Mahabaleshwar, Maharashtra, and flows into the Bay of Bengal through Andhra Pradesh, not through Chhattisgarh/Odisha.

 

• Godavari (Option 3): Also originates near Trimbakeshwar, Maharashtra, flowing eastward into the Bay of Bengal, unrelated to Sihawa, Chhattisgarh.

 

• Cauvery (Option 4): Originates at Talakaveri, Karnataka (Western Ghats), and flows through Tamil Nadu into the Bay of Bengal — a South Indian river unrelated to Chhattisgarh.

question: Which of the following programmes of the Government of India aims to provide connectivity to unconnected habitations as part of a poverty reduction strategy?
option_1: Prime Minister Rural Development Fellows Scheme
solution_text:
The correct answer is Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Pradhan Mantri Gram Sadak Yojana (PMGSY) was launched on 25 December 2000 with the objective of providing all-weather road connectivity to unconnected rural habitations, as part of the government's poverty reduction strategy. (प्रधानमंत्री ग्राम सड़क योजना — असंबद्ध बस्तियों को सड़क संपर्क)

 

• It is a Centrally Sponsored Scheme under the Ministry of Rural Development, funded partly through the accumulated diesel cess in the Central Road Fund.

 

• Improved rural connectivity under PMGSY facilitates better access to markets, healthcare, and education, directly contributing to rural poverty alleviation.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• PMGSY-II and the PMGSY-III (for connecting rural areas to schools, health centres and market hubs) are later phases expanding the original scheme.

 

• PMGSY initially targeted habitations with a population of 500+ (250+ in special category/hilly/tribal states).

 

NOTE

 

• Prime Minister Rural Development Fellows Scheme (Option 1): Deploys young professionals in backward districts for development work; unrelated to road/habitation connectivity.

 

• Swarnjayanti Gram Swarozgar Yojana (Option 2): A self-employment scheme for rural poor (later subsumed under NRLM), not focused on connectivity.

 

• National Rural Livelihoods Mission (Option 4): Aims at poverty reduction through building sustainable livelihoods and self-help groups, not through road connectivity.

question: Who is credited with creating the popular Raga Miya Ki Malhar?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Tansen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Raga Miya Ki Malhar, a monsoon raga believed to have the power to invoke rain, is credited to Tansen, one of the Navratnas (nine gems) in the court of Mughal Emperor Akbar. (मियां की मल्हार — तानसेन)

 

• Tansen was a legendary Hindustani classical vocalist and composer, renowned for creating several ragas including Miyan ki Todi, Miyan ki Malhar, and Darbari Kanada.

 

• He was trained under Swami Haridas and later became a disciple of Muhammad Ghaus, before joining Akbar's court around 1562.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Tansen Samman, a prestigious award for classical musicians, is given annually by the Madhya Pradesh government in his honour, and the Tansen Music Festival is held at his tomb in Gwalior.

 

• Tansen is considered the founder of several gharanas (musical lineages) of Hindustani classical music, including the Senia Gharana.

 

NOTE

 

• Amir Khusrau (Option 2): Credited with developing instruments like the sitar and tabla and musical forms like qawwali and khyal, not Miyan ki Malhar.

 

• Meera Bai (Option 3): A renowned Bhakti-era poet-saint known for devotional songs to Lord Krishna, not associated with creating this raga.

 

• Zakir Hussain (Option 4): A contemporary tabla maestro, not connected to the creation of classical ragas like Miyan ki Malhar.

question: Name a unit designed for wet and dry bulb thermometers to protect temperature sensors from being affected by direct or reflected sunlight.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Stevenson screen.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• A Stevenson screen is a louvred, white-painted wooden or plastic enclosure used to house meteorological instruments, including wet and dry bulb thermometers, shielding them from direct sunlight, precipitation, and radiation while allowing free air circulation for accurate readings. (स्टीवेंसन स्क्रीन — मौसम उपकरणों की सुरक्षा हेतु बॉक्स)

 

• It was designed by the Scottish engineer Thomas Stevenson (father of author Robert Louis Stevenson) in the 1860s.

 

• The screen's louvred sides and white colour minimise heat absorption, ensuring that temperature and humidity readings reflect the actual ambient air conditions rather than being skewed by direct/reflected sunlight.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Instruments commonly housed in a Stevenson screen include dry-bulb and wet-bulb thermometers, maximum-minimum thermometers, and hygrometers.

 

• Stevenson screens are typically mounted at a standard height of about 1.25 metres above the ground for consistency in meteorological observations worldwide.

 

NOTE

 

• Skywarn screen (Option 2): Not a real meteorological instrument enclosure; "Skywarn" is actually a US weather-spotter volunteer programme name, used here as a distractor.

 

• Clarinet screen (Option 3): Not a meteorological term; a fabricated distractor unrelated to weather instruments.

 

• Cardinal screen (Option 4): Not a meteorological term; a fabricated distractor unrelated to weather instruments.

question: Who among the following sportspersons was NOT awarded the Arjuna Award in 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Arpinder Singh.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• The Arjuna Award 2022 was conferred on badminton players Lakshya Sen and HS Prannoy, and judoka Sushila Devi Likmabam, among other athletes, for their outstanding sporting achievements. (अर्जुन पुरस्कार 2022 — लक्ष्य सेन, सुशीला देवी, एच.एस. प्रणय)

 

• Arpinder Singh, the triple jumper who famously won gold at the 2018 Asian Games ending India's 48-year medal drought in the event, was not among the 2022 Arjuna Award recipients.

 

• The Arjuna Award is conferred by the Ministry of Youth Affairs and Sports for consistently outstanding performance in national and international sporting events over the preceding four years.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 4.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Major Dhyan Chand Khel Ratna Award, India's highest sporting honour, was given to table tennis player Achanta Sharath Kamal in 2022.

 

• Arjuna Awardees also receive a bronze statuette of Arjuna, a certificate, and a cash prize as part of the honour.

 

NOTE

 

• Lakshya Sen (Option 1): Received the Arjuna Award 2022 for his achievements in badminton.

 

• Sushila Devi (Option 2): Received the Arjuna Award 2022 for her achievements in judo.

 

• HS Prannoy (Option 3): Received the Arjuna Award 2022 for his achievements in badminton.

question: Which article of the Indian Constitution deals with the formation of New States and Alteration of Areas, Boundaries or names of existing States?
solution_text:
The correct answer is 3.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Article 3 of the Indian Constitution empowers Parliament to form new States and to alter the areas, boundaries, or names of existing States by a simple majority law. (अनुच्छेद 3 — नए राज्यों का गठन)

 

• Under Article 3, a bill for this purpose can only be introduced in Parliament on the recommendation of the President, and the President must refer it to the concerned State Legislature for its views within a specified period.

 

• This provision reflects India's character as an "indestructible Union of destructible States", as Parliament can reorganise state boundaries without requiring the state's consent.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Article 1 declares India as a "Union of States," while Article 2 empowers Parliament to admit or establish new States into the Union.

 

• The States Reorganisation Act, 1956, based largely on linguistic lines, is a major historical exercise of the powers under Article 3.

 

NOTE

 

• Article 6 (Option 1): Deals with citizenship rights of persons who migrated to India from Pakistan at the commencement of the Constitution.

 

• Article 4 (Option 2): Provides that laws made under Articles 2 and 3 (for admission/formation of States) shall contain supplementary, incidental, and consequential provisions, and are not to be treated as constitutional amendments under Article 368.

 

• Article 5 (Option 4): Deals with citizenship at the commencement of the Constitution for persons domiciled in India.

question: Which of the following compounds having the molecular formula C2H is derived from the hydride of acetylene?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Ethynyl.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ethynyl (or acetylenyl), with molecular formula C₂H, is the functional group/radical derived by removing one hydrogen atom from acetylene (C₂H₂), the simplest alkyne. (एथाइनिल — एसिटिलीन से व्युत्पन्न)

 

• It is represented as -C≡CH and is the simplest alkynyl group, retaining the triple bond characteristic of acetylene.

 

• Ethynyl groups are found in various organic compounds and are important in organic synthesis for constructing carbon-carbon triple bonds.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Acetylene (C₂H₂), also called ethyne, is the simplest member of the alkyne family, characterised by a carbon-carbon triple bond.

 

• Substituted acetylene derivatives are widely used in industrial synthesis, welding (oxy-acetylene torches), and as precursors for polymers.

 

NOTE

 

• Propargyl (Option 2): Refers to the -CH₂-C≡CH group (from propyne), with molecular formula C₃H₃, not C₂H.

 

• Vinyl (Option 3): Refers to the -CH=CH₂ group, derived from ethylene (an alkene), not from acetylene.

 

• Allyl (Option 4): Refers to the -CH₂-CH=CH₂ group, derived from propene (an alkene), unrelated to acetylene.

question: Who among the following was given the charge of looking after the imperial household during the Mughal administration?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Mir Saman.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Mir Saman (also called Khan-i-Saman) was the high-ranking Mughal official in charge of the imperial household, including the royal karkhanas (workshops), stores, and purchases for the emperor's establishment. (मीर सामान — शाही घराने का प्रभारी)

 

• He supervised the manufacture and procurement of items for the royal household, such as textiles, jewellery, and other luxury goods, through various state-controlled karkhanas.

 

• This post was typically held by a noble of high trust and status, given its proximity to the emperor's personal and domestic affairs.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• The Mughal administrative structure included key officials like the Wazir/Diwan (finance), Mir Bakshi (military pay and personnel), Sadr-us-Sudur (religious/charitable grants), and Qazi-ul-Quzat (chief judge).

 

• The karkhanas under Mir Saman's supervision produced everything from clothing to weapons for the royal household.

 

NOTE

 

• Mir Bahri (Option 2): In charge of the navy/admiralty and river transport under the Mughals, not the imperial household.

 

• Mir Bakshi (Option 3): The head of the military department, responsible for the recruitment, muster, and pay of the mansabdars/army, not household affairs.

 

• 'Mir-e-aatish' (Option 4): The officer in charge of the artillery (top-khana) in the Mughal army, unrelated to the imperial household.

question: Who among the following won the gold medal at International Weightlifting Federation's youth world championship in June 2022?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Gurunaidu Sanapathi.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Gurunaidu Sanapathi, a weightlifter from Andhra Pradesh, won the gold medal in the men's 55 kg category at the IWF (International Weightlifting Federation) Youth World Championships, held in Heraklion, Greece, in June 2022. (गुरुनायडु सनपति — भारोत्तोलन में स्वर्ण पदक, जून 2022)

 

• With this win, he became India's first weightlifter to win a gold medal at the Youth World Weightlifting Championships.

 

• He achieved this feat with a combined lift total in the snatch and clean & jerk categories, defeating competitors from several countries.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 2.

 

Additional Information

 

• India's weightlifting programme has produced other notable achievers, including Mirabai Chanu, who won a silver medal at the Tokyo 2020 Olympics.

 

• The International Weightlifting Federation (IWF) is the global governing body for the sport of weightlifting, overseeing world championships across senior, junior, and youth categories.

 

NOTE

 

• Devang Desai (Option 1): Not the gold medallist at the 2022 IWF Youth World Championships; used here as a distractor.

 

• Devineni Srikanth (Option 3): Not the gold medallist at the 2022 IWF Youth World Championships; used here as a distractor.

 

• Fajaru Nasik (Option 4): Not the gold medallist at the 2022 IWF Youth World Championships; used here as a distractor.

question: Ranjumoni Saikia was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award 2019 for her contribution to which classical dance?
solution_text:
The correct answer is Sattriya.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Ranjumoni Saikia, a noted exponent from Assam, was awarded the Sangeet Natak Akademi Award in 2019 for her contribution to Sattriya, the classical dance form native to Assam. (सत्रीया नृत्य — असम, संगीत नाटक अकादमी पुरस्कार 2019)

 

• Sattriya originated in the satras (Vaishnavite monasteries) of Assam, founded by the saint-reformer Srimanta Sankardev in the 15th-16th century.

 

• It was accorded the status of a classical dance form of India by the Sangeet Natak Akademi in 2000, becoming the 8th classical dance form recognised in the country.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 3.

 

Additional Information

 

• Other classical dance forms of India include Bharatanatyam (Tamil Nadu), Kathak (North India), Kathakali and Mohiniyattam (Kerala), Kuchipudi (Andhra Pradesh), Odissi (Odisha), and Manipuri (Manipur).

 

• The Sangeet Natak Akademi, India's national academy for music, dance and drama, is the highest body conferring national recognition for performing artists.

 

NOTE

 

• Kuchipudi (Option 1): A classical dance form native to Andhra Pradesh, not Assam.

 

• Mohiniyattam (Option 2): A classical dance form native to Kerala, characterised by graceful, swaying movements.

 

• Chhau (Option 4): A semi-classical dance form associated with Odisha, Jharkhand, and West Bengal, not classified among the awardee's specialisation here.

question: Name the transuranium element with atomic number 106, created by bombarding californium-249 with oxygen-18 nuclei.
solution_text:
The correct answer is Seaborgium.

 

IMPORTANT POINTS

 

• Seaborgium (Sg), a synthetic transuranium element with atomic number 106, was first created in 1974 by bombarding californium-249 with oxygen-18 nuclei at Lawrence Berkeley National Laboratory. (सीबोर्जियम — परमाणु क्रमांक 106)

 

• It was named in honour of the American nuclear chemist Glenn T. Seaborg, a key figure in the discovery of several transuranium elements.

 

• Seaborgium is highly radioactive with no stable isotopes and is produced only in minute quantities in laboratory settings for research purposes.

 

Therefore, the correct answer is Option 1.

 

Additional Information

 

• Transuranium elements are elements with atomic numbers greater than 92 (uranium); they are all synthetic/man-made and radioactive.

 

• Seaborg is also the only person to have an element named after him during his lifetime.

 

NOTE

 

• Dubnium (Option 2): Atomic number 105, named after Dubna, Russia, the site of the Joint Institute for Nuclear Research.

 

• Hassium (Option 3): Atomic number 108, named after the German state of Hesse (Hassia in Latin).

 

• Copernicium (Option 4): Atomic number 112, named after the astronomer Nicolaus Copernicus.
